question: How does the will-power give rise to the phoneme ya?
premises: The will-power exists in stirred and unstirred modes.
In a certain condition it turns toward an element of a different power.
This turning produces a distinct phonemic identity.
inference: When the will-power inclines toward another power, it manifests as the phoneme ya.
uncertainties: The 'different power' is not named explicitly in this verse.
plain_english: The will-power, twofold as stirred and unstirred, turns toward an element of another power and thereby becomes the phoneme ya.
